newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Zaire refugees return voluntarily from Tanzania.
newsitem.headline: Zaire refugees return voluntarily from Tanzania.

text.p: A total of 6,000 refugees who fled the former Zaire for Tanzania's Kigoma region have repatriated voluntarily, a senior aid official said on Monday.
The bulk of the refugees were unregistered with the U.N. refugee agency (UNHCR) and were living in villages along the east shore of Lake Tanganyika, said the Kigoma-based repatriation official.
A second group living in UNHCR camps escaped and returned to homes around Uvira, at the northwest tip of the lake.
"What I can say from the movement of boats, is that people are leaving on their own. About 6,000 or so have gone back in small groups," said the aid official who declined to be named.
"These individuals were staying in villages and mixing with the local population and have now returned. There are also a few cases of people who have escaped from the camps," the official said.

Tanzania plays host to about 100,000 refugees from the Democratic Republic of Congo who fled to Kigoma to escape a seven-month civil war that brought Laurent Kabila to power and ousted former president Mobutu Sese Seko.
More refugees set off daily for the 12-hour boat journey, said a second official.
"People are going back each day unnofficially. These people are finding the money for a ticket -- about $20 and just taking the boat," he said, asking not to be named.
The UNHCR said on Monday about 5,000 registered Congolese refugees, many of whom worked as civil servants under Mobutu, wanted to return home officially.
